headline: Registration and Charter Coordination for Ellesmere Island
reservation: Access to Quttinirpaaq requires registration with Parks Canada and coordination with specialized charter flight operators due to the extreme remote location. While there is no daily entry fee system, visitors must obtain a mandatory orientation and ensure all permit paperwork is finalized through the park office before departing Resolute. Systems for polar travel are subject to change, so verify current compliance requirements with the official agency.

days.title: High Arctic Tundra and Lake Hazen
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Tanquary Fiord base

stops.name: Lake Hazen
stops.detail: Observe the unique thermal oasis of the world's most northerly large lake, where the surrounding mountains provide a sheltered microclimate.

stops.name: Tanquary Fiord
stops.detail: Explore the designated landing site and base camp area, which serves as the primary hub for research and visitor registration.

days.driving: Allow all day for regional air transfers or local trekking; conditions vary wildly by weather.
days.note: Permafrost and extreme weather may alter flight schedules without notice.

days.title: Glacial Landscapes and Archaeological Sites

stops.name: Henrietta Nesmith Glacier
stops.detail: View the massive ice tongues flowing from the British Empire Range toward the Lake Hazen basin.

stops.name: Kettle Lake
stops.detail: Discover the geological formations and evidence of Paleo-Inuit history in this rugged northern interior.

days.driving: Walking only; allow several hours for short traverses over uneven tundra.
days.note: Wildlife protocols for muskox and polar bears must be strictly followed.

days.title: Northern Fiord Exploration

stops.name: Fort Conger
stops.detail: Visit the historic site of early Arctic expeditions, where the remains of wooden huts illustrate the challenges of 19th-century exploration.

stops.name: Ward Hunt Island
stops.detail: Experience the northernmost point of the park, characterized by ancient ice shelves and seasonal scientific research stations.

days.driving: Internal travel requires pre-arranged charter aircraft or long-distance ski trekking.
days.note: Fog frequently impacts visibility and flight safety in the fiord regions.

intel.title: No Public Roads
intel.text: There are no roads or parking facilities within the park boundaries. All logistics are managed via air charter from Resolute or Grise Fiord.

intel.title: Satellite Communication Only
intel.text: Cellular and traditional radio signals are non-existent in this region. Visitors must carry a satellite phone or emergency beacon and verify its function before departure.

intel.title: Gateway Fuel Points
intel.text: The last reliable fuel source is in Resolute; no fuel is available for purchase within the park. Expedition groups must cache all necessary stove and aircraft fuel according to strict environmental regulations.

intel.title: The Midnight Sun
intel.text: The park experiences 24-hour daylight during the summer season, which can affect sleep cycles. Plan movements based on weather windows rather than traditional clock hours.

intel.title: Charter Windows
intel.text: Entry is restricted by the short summer melt season when aircraft can land on the tundra. Always confirm the current status of the landing strips at Tanquary Fiord and Lake Hazen.

plan.arrival: Arrive in Resolute for gear check, mandatory Parks Canada orientation, and final grocery stocking before the charter flight north.
plan.vehicle: Wheeled vehicles are not permitted; local travel is strictly via bush plane, ski, or foot. Check charter weight limits.
plan.goldenHour: Tanquary Fiord viewpoints offer continuous soft light in summer, though traditional sunset does not occur.
